title: Asymmetric burst + soak orchestrator for Dedicated capacity regression benchmarking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an orchestrated load-harness (PulseLoad) that runs a long-duration soak with configurable asymmetric burst patterns on Dedicated GPU pools to validate autoscaler stability and p95 regressions. The harness should exercise realistic production-like mixes (chat/text-gen/embedding backends), include KV cache warmup and cold-start windows, and emit Prometheus metrics for tokens/sec, p95, error rates, and autoscaler decisions. This ticket covers designing the asymmetric burst profile, implementing the orchestrator and runners, wiring the metric exporters, and adding a regression detector that alerts on statistically significant p95 increases or sustained tokens/sec drops.
test_plan_summary: Run nightly 4-hour soak with 45-min steady baseline at 1500 tokens/sec on medium models, inject 6 asymmetric bursts (30s, 60s, 180s) with peak up to 12k tokens/sec, and validate autoscaler reacts within configured SLO without oscillation. Repeat with cold cache (service restart) to validate warmup behavior. Capture golden baseline and compare via EWMA and non-parametric change-detection to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run scheduled asymmetric burst+soak scenarios against Dedicated pools and produce complete Prometheus time series and an artifacts tarball (logs/trace/summary.json).
Regression detector runs automatically post-job and flags runs where p95 increases > 15% vs baseline with p < 0.01 (Mann-Whitney U) or where sustained tokens/sec drop > 20% for > 10 minutes.
Autoscaler behavior validation: no >3 oscillations (scale up/down) inside a 10-minute window for any single burst; scale events recorded in exported metrics and traces.
Include a reproducible 'cold-start' variant that restarts runtime to validate KV cache warmup profile and emits warmup curve to artifacts.
Documentation and runbook: how to add new burst profiles, interpret regression detector output, and annotate false positives.
Smoke CI job created that runs a 30-minute mini-version of the harness on PRs touching serving runtime or autoscaler config.
steps: Design asymmetric burst profile DSL (duration, peak_tokens, ramp_up_ms, decay_shape, interburst_gap) and document in Confluence.
Implement PulseLoad runner in go/python to produce token-level traffic and label requests with scenario metadata.
Add orchestration manifest (K8s Job / Argo Workflow) to run multi-tenant scenarios across Dedicated pools and capture pod-level traces.
Expose and standardize metric names in runtime to match metrics_monitored list and add a lightweight exporter for PulseLoad client-side metrics.
Implement regression-detector service: ingest run summary, compute EWMA and MWU comparisons vs baseline, and publish findings to Slack and a DB table for historical tracking.
Create dashboard in Console for asymmetric-burst runs showing tokens/sec, p95, replica count, and KV hit-ratio with event markers for burst boundaries.
Write runbook and add CI smoke test and nightly scheduled job definition.
progress_updates: 2026-02-02: Spike completed on burst DSL and initial YAML schema for profiles; defined fields and default decay shapes (linear, exponential, plateau).
2026-02-04: Prototype PulseLoad PoC in Python that can replay a recorded production trace and drive peak tokens/sec; emits basic metrics to Prometheus pushgateway.

2026-02-08: Orchestration manifest PR opened (github.com/redwood/replay-harness/pull/412) that wires a multi-pod job with init steps for KV warmup. CI failing on RBAC for exporter service account — blocked by infra fix ENG-70288.

2026-02-11: Regression detector basic implementation done; uses EWMA for drift detection and Mann-Whitney U for distribution change; now needs tuning of sensitivity and false-positive suppression heuristics.

notes: Aim to minimize false positives by combining effect-size rules with statistical tests. For initial rollout run detector in 'report-only' mode for 2 weeks and review signals before enabling alerting. Keep artifacts retention to 90 days for forensic analyses.
